findings.text: SMI blocking query and special nested exit classifier are externally visible for use by host SMI handling and nested exit dispatch.

SMI is reported blocked whenever the global interrupt flag is clear; otherwise blocked status follows whether the virtual CPU currently resides in system management mode, honoring the cited hardware manual response rule.
Whether a system management interrupt causes a nested exit depends only on the cached L1 control request for that intercept.

Special exit routing sends external interrupts, non-maskable interrupts and nested page faults to the host, sends intercepted exceptions plus asynchronous page fault traps plus L2 translation flush hypercalls to the host, and otherwise continues normal nested processing.

Cached to architectural control transfer starts from a cleared area and carries intercept tables plus permission bases, time offset, address space and flush controls, interrupt state and injection, exit reporting, next instruction pointer, nested paging root and pause tuning, while cleanliness and enlightenment markers stay unchanged.

Nested state query reports SVM format with size and status flags for guest mode, pending nested run and global interrupt flag, includes the L1 VMCB address and guest page attribute when active, returns the full VMCB control and host save images to userspace, and supports size probing when no CPU context is supplied.

Nested state restore only accepts SVM format with recognized flags, refuses disabled virtualization with active nesting, SMM guest mode, invalid VMCB address or truncated payload, and refuses inconsistent control, host save or page attribute values before changing any mode.

Accepted restore installs the supplied VMCB address, control and host save images, selects the secondary VMCB, refreshes derived control, marks translation state dirty, reloads the paging root, and schedules deferred updates for permission bitmaps, virtualized interrupts and nested pages; a payload without guest mode simply leaves nesting and refreshes the global interrupt flag.

Deferred nested page completion refreshes PAE directory pointers according to paging mode, tolerating userspace-supplied values in shadow mode, and then requires successful permission bitmap merge and hypervisor assist validation.

Nested address translation requires an active nested memory context, elevates walks to user privilege unless guest transparency is enabled, and delegates final guest-physical to host-physical conversion to the nested walker with caller access rights and fault reporting.

SVM nested dispatch table aggregates leave, address translation, exception classification, event polling, triple fault, deferred page completion, state save and restore, and synthetic post-flush exit injection.
Performance and confidential-computing modules tag diagnostics with their module name prefix.
Performance selector kind distinguishes counter access from event selection with two successive values beginning at zero.
General counter lookup rejects indexes at or beyond the configured architectural count and otherwise returns the corresponding slot.

General MSR to counter resolution requires core counting capability for extended pairs, distinguishes control from count by address parity and range, enforces matching access kind for legacy ranges, and yields absent for unknown addresses or disabled version.
Early read validation fails indexes outside the architectural general count, while index translation for read requests directly forwards to general counter lookup.
MSR index to counter resolution prefers the count view and falls back to the selection view.

MSR acceptance gates legacy ranges on any version, extended and global control ranges on newer versions or capabilities, bounds extended indexes by configured count, and otherwise follows mapped counter existence.

MSR access returns live counter content for count addresses and stored selection for event addresses, installs masked event selections with host-only cleared and guest-only enforced while tracking mode-specific enablement and requesting reprogramming on change, and reports unhandled addresses distinctly.

Refresh selects version two only with second-generation monitoring support and otherwise version one, derives count from guest capability data with host limit clamping, prepares global reservation masks, fixed wide counter width, reserved selection mask with mediation adjustment, and empty fixed-counter configuration.
Initialization prepares every maximum general slot with general type, owning CPU linkage, positional index and cleared configuration.

Mediated handover is available only on hosts with at least version two; entry discards stale host overflow indications and installs guest status and enablement, while exit disables hardware counting, preserves status for the guest and clears hardware indications.

Mediation-aware disablement never applies without mediation, ignores empty host-guest selection, disables any selective counting when virtualization is off, treats dual selection as always enabled, and otherwise compares the requested personality against current guest execution.

AMD performance dispatch table aggregates translation, validation, access, lifecycle, mediation and mode-disablement handlers together with event field position, counter limits, base addresses, stride and global control identity.
Communication protocol supports versions one through two inclusive, with hypervisor features advertising nested paging security plus application processor creation.
Generic guest to hypervisor error for secure nested paging is the all-ones 32-bit value.
Secondary processor reset hold modes are none, event-driven and register-protocol with values zero, one and two respectively.
Initial save area for secure launch attestation is at 0xFFFFFFFFF000, one page below the top of the low canonical range.

Admissible secure policy mask combines version minor and major, multithreading, reserved-must-be-one, debug, single socket, interconnect permission, memory encryption strength, power control, memory hiding and swap disable controls.

Master switches for memory encryption, encrypted state and secure nested paging default to enabled in post-init immutable storage, together with ciphertext-hiding identifier count, supported policy bits, supported save-area features and encryption bit position.
Secure identifier bitmap allocation is protected by a dedicated mutex.
User-supplied nested headers and VMCB images are length, format, flag, address and consistency checked before mode changes, and user copy plus allocation faults abort without partial commit.
Performance index handling bounds all accesses to configured counts with speculative-safe indexing and early rejection, and event selection updates mask reserved bits.

Misuse such as page fixups outside guest mode, translation without nested tables, or reprogramming checks without the common enable bit triggers warnings, and merge, assist or directory load failures propagate as operation failure.
